failure_modes: If the observed-node shape_yy/shape_xx contrast is selection-enrichment rather than an absolute geometric target, the blend may displace surrounding coordinates without improving final predicted affinity.
Because the landmark contrast is non-monotone with multiple sign changes, a larger blend could reverse the sign of the integrated shape effect versus the static incumbent.
No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied, so the expected advantage is relative selection evidence and cannot be confirmed as absolute affinity benefit.
rationale: Analyst's endpoint contrasts show the surviving high-low integrated effects are shape (second-moment) descriptors (shape_yy, shape_xx) with zero positive batches, while centroid translation terms are near-null; the continuous landmark contrasts are non-monotone with no accepted polynomial, so only observed-node interpolation is licensed. The registered temporal_teacher recipe changes only regional attention at observed score nodes using the same static teachers and shared FLOWR endpoint VJP, which is exactly the coordinate observable H001 targets. Among the offered temporal_teacher_blend values, C009 (0.25) is the smallest non-zero dose: it shifts attention toward the observed-node contrast while keeping the static incumbent dominant, so the predicted response is a modest shift of the endpoint pointcloud toward the favorable shape direction with bounded risk of displacing surrounding coordinates. Larger blends (C010, C011) would let the non-monotone observed-node curve dominate and risk sign reversals in shape_yy/shape_xx, so they are not chosen. No temperature, teacher provenance, or velocity target is altered; teacher_neighbors and pointcloud_delta_A remain at incumbent values.
